ai.definition: RAG pipelines, or Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines, integrate retrieval-based models with generative AI to enhance the accuracy and contextual richness of responses in knowledge management systems.
ai.howItWorks: These pipelines first retrieve relevant documents or passages from a database or corpus using a retrieval model. Then, a generative model is used to generate a response that incorporates the retrieved information while adding contextually rich details.
ai.problemSolved: Improving the accuracy and contextual richness of responses in complex information retrieval tasks, thereby enhancing user satisfaction and efficiency.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training both retrieval-based and generative models, integrating them into a pipeline, and fine-tuning to ensure optimal performance.
ai.buildProcess: Models are built using large datasets for training. The retrieval model is first trained on a corpus of documents to understand the context and structure. The generative model is then trained to generate coherent responses based on the retrieved information.
ai.costDrivers: Data acquisition, computational resources, and expert labor for model development and fine-tuning are key cost drivers.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to see widespread adoption in knowledge management systems as it matures and becomes more refined.
ai.regulation: Regulations will likely focus on data privacy, bias mitigation, and ensuring the ethical use of AI in knowledge management applications.
ai.risks: Potential risks include data privacy concerns, model biases, and the need for continuous updates to maintain accuracy and relevance.
ai.profitability: Profitability is expected to increase as adoption grows, but initial costs may limit profitability until economies of scale are achieved.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments will likely focus on improving model performance, reducing bias, and integrating more advanced natural language processing techniques.

glossary.def: A method that combines retrieval-based models with generative AI to enhance the accuracy and contextual richness of responses.
A machine learning model designed to retrieve relevant documents or passages from a database based on user queries.
A machine learning model that generates coherent text based on the retrieved information and context provided by the retrieval model.

subsystems.name: Ingestion and parsing
subsystems.role: Turns heterogeneous source documents into clean, machine-readable text.

subsystems.name: Chunking and embedding
subsystems.role: Splits text into retrievable passages and converts each into a vector.

subsystems.name: Vector index
subsystems.role: Stores embeddings so that similar passages can be found quickly.

subsystems.name: Retriever and re-ranker
subsystems.role: Fetches candidate passages and selects the most relevant ones for the query.

subsystems.name: Generator
subsystems.role: Composes a grounded answer from the retrieved passages.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and evaluation
subsystems.role: Wires the stages together and measures whether answers are faithful and useful.

buildSteps.title: Connect and extract
buildSteps.detail: Attach the pipeline to document stores, wikis, databases or web sources, then extract raw text and strip navigation, headers and other clutter.

buildSteps.title: Parse and chunk
buildSteps.detail: Split the extracted text into passages of a few hundred tokens, with slight overlap and preserved headings, tables and source metadata so context is not lost at the boundaries.

buildSteps.title: Embed passages
buildSteps.detail: Run every chunk through an embedding model to produce a vector that represents its meaning.

buildSteps.title: Index vectors
buildSteps.detail: Insert the vectors and their metadata into a vector database and build an approximate nearest-neighbour index for fast search.

buildSteps.title: Set up retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Combine semantic vector search with keyword search, then add a re-ranking model to pick the handful of passages most likely to answer the user's question.

buildSteps.title: Design the generation prompt
buildSteps.detail: Instruct the language model to answer only from the supplied context, to say when the context is insufficient, and to cite the passages it used.

buildSteps.title: Run queries end to end
buildSteps.detail: At question time, embed the query, retrieve and re-rank passages, pass them to the generator, and return a cited answer.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and tune
buildSteps.detail: Measure retrieval recall and answer faithfulness on a labelled question set, then adjust chunk size, embedding model, re-ranker and prompt until quality is acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Serve the pipeline behind an API, log queries and failures, and watch for stale documents, drifted embedding models and changing user needs.

prerequisites.why: The generation step needs a model capable of synthesising an answer from supplied passages.
They convert passages and queries into vectors so semantic similarity can be computed.

prerequisites.tech: Vector databases and approximate nearest-neighbour search
prerequisites.why: They make it practical to search millions of passages in milliseconds.
Much enterprise knowledge sits in PDFs, scans and slide decks that must be converted to text first.
Measuring faithfulness, relevance and attribution is still an active research area, so quality assurance remains partly manual.

pathway.milestone: Basic retrieve-then-generate pipelines widely deployed in search and support tools
pathway.unlocks: Answers grounded in an organisation's own documents rather than the model's training data alone.

pathway.milestone: Hybrid retrieval, re-ranking and strict citation grounding become standard
pathway.unlocks: Lower hallucination rates and answers that users can trace back to sources.

pathway.milestone: Agentic RAG with query rewriting, multi-step retrieval and tool use
pathway.unlocks: Handling of complex, multi-part questions that no single search can answer.

pathway.milestone: Continuous, self-evaluating knowledge pipelines that detect stale content and retrain retrieval components
pathway.unlocks: Knowledge systems that stay accurate as underlying documents change.
